description: [DEEP] Session handling — verify clearing auth cookies redirects to login gracefully

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from '/home/ouroborous/code/phronex-test-runner/.tmp/comc-trunk-superadmin-state.json'. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/dashboard. Verify the page loads with ComC content (not a login redirect). Take a screenshot to confirm an authenticated session.

Verify the ComC backend independently enforces authentication. Use browser_network_request to call GET http://localhost:8004/api/v1/agents with no Authorization header. The response MUST be 401 (or 403) — NOT 200. This verifies the backend does not serve protected data to unauthenticated callers regardless of the portal session state.

Verify the portal proxy enforces session authentication. Use browser_network_request (NOT a browser tab — browser_network_request does NOT send browser session cookies) to call GET http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/agents with NO Cookie header and NO Authorization header. The portal's Auth.js middleware should detect the missing session and return 307 (redirect to login) or 401. PASS if response status is 307, 401, or 403. FAIL if response is 200 with JSON data — that would mean the proxy is serving protected ComC data to unauthenticated callers. Note: browser_network_request is correct here because it sends a raw HTTP request without the browser session cookies, simulating an unauthenticated caller.

Test the portal signout flow. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/api/auth/signout via browser_navigate. If a confirmation page appears, accept it. Then navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/dashboard. Verify the portal redirects to http://localhost:3002/auth/login rather than showing protected ComC content. Take a screenshot showing the login form.

Verify the login page is shown after signout. The page must show an email input and a password input. Mark passed if the redirect to login is clean. Mark failed if a blank page, 500 error, or ComC dashboard content is shown instead of the login form.

description: [DEEP] Platform Overview — verify page loads and API returns correct structure for superadmin

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from '/home/ouroborous/code/phronex-test-runner/.tmp/comc-trunk-superadmin-state.json' using the browser storage state tool. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/platform-overview. Verify the page loads without a login redirect or generic 404 error.

Verify the platform overview page's access control behavior. Take a screenshot of the current page state. PASS CONDITION: the page either (a) shows a 403 Forbidden message (correct — the QA account has a product grant but not platform superadmin access, so a 403 is the correct and expected response), OR (b) renders the page with tabs (Strategy, IP Scores, Reuse Matrix, Actions) visible. FAIL CONDITION: page shows a 500 error, a blank white screen, or a login redirect. A 403 message means the auth system is working correctly — mark it as passed and note '403 expected for non-platform-superadmin QA account'.

CONDITIONAL — only execute if step 2 result was that the page LOADED WITH TABS (not a 403 page). If step 2 showed a 403 error, mark this step as passed and skip. If tabs were visible: click the IP Scores tab and verify it shows either IP score entries with progress bars, or an empty state message. Click the Reuse Matrix tab and verify it loads. Navigate back to Strategy tab. This step verifies tab navigation works when a platform superadmin account is used.

Verify the platform-overview API access control. Use browser_network_request to call GET http://localhost:8004/api/v1/admin/platform-overview with no Authorization header. Verify the response is 401 (unauthorized). This confirms the backend enforces authentication on platform-level admin routes.

Use browser_network_request to call GET http://localhost:8004/api/v1/admin/platform-overview with Authorization header 'Bearer invalid-token'. Verify the response is 401. This confirms the backend validates token signatures and does not serve platform intel to callers with forged tokens. Mark passed if both step 4 and step 5 return 401.

description: [DEEP] AI Explainability — verify decisions, approvals, and explainability pages load

steps.description: Load saved superadmin session from '/home/ouroborous/code/phronex-test-runner/.tmp/comc-trunk-superadmin-state.json' using the browser storage state tool. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/explainability. Verify the page loads without 500 error or login redirect. The page should show an AI Explainability heading and a sub-tab bar with Feed, Trails, Anomalies, Stats, and Insights tabs.

Verify the explainability page renders or fails gracefully. Take a screenshot of the Feed tab content. PASS CONDITION: the page shows either (A) a list of AI decision records, (B) an empty state message like 'No decisions yet', or (C) an error state/message (acceptable — known infrastructure constraint: the decisions backend returns 500 for the command-centre product slug because phronex-auth EC2 is running an older phronex-common that predates command-centre ProductSlug support; this is a phronex-auth deployment gap, not a ComC bug). FAIL CONDITION ONLY: the entire portal crashes or the page shows a login redirect. Document whatever state you observe and mark as passed.

Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/decisions. Verify the decisions log page loads. Check for either decision entries with title/date/outcome or an empty state. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/approvals. Verify the approvals page loads — it may show pending approvals or an empty queue.

Verify the phronex-auth decisions proxy route is reachable. Use browser_network_request to call GET http://localhost:3002/api/admin/auth/admin/decisions?product=content-companion&limit=5. Verify the response is 200 OK with a JSON object containing an 'items' array (may be empty). NOTE: Do NOT use product=command-centre — phronex-auth EC2 returns 500 for that slug because it is running an older phronex-common version. Use content-companion as a proxy test to confirm the decisions route infrastructure is working end-to-end. A 404 would indicate the proxy route itself is missing. Mark passed if 200 with items array, mark failed only on 404 (route missing) or network error.

Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/ethos. Verify it loads with an ethos policy or empty state. Navigate back to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/dashboard and verify the session is still active (dashboard shows content, not login redirect). Take a final screenshot.

description: [DEEP] Accountability links — create, list, and verify the accountability portal page

steps.description: Load saved CEO session from '/home/ouroborous/code/phronex-test-runner/.tmp/comc-trunk-ceo-state.json' using the browser storage state tool. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/accountability. Verify the page loads without 500 error or login redirect.

Verify the accountability page renders correctly: either (A) a list of accountability links showing partner names, initiative descriptions, and link status, or (B) an empty state explaining that accountability links connect you with a partner for initiative tracking. No blank screen or raw error.

Verify the accountability API via browser_network_request: GET http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/accountability/links. The response must be an array (possibly empty). If 404, the accountability endpoint is missing — mark as defect. If 403, the CEO session is being rejected — mark as defect.

Test creating an accountability link via API: use browser_network_request to POST http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/accountability/links with body {"partner_email": "partner@example.com", "initiative_description": "Test initiative from JourneyHawk"}. Verify the response status is 201 or 200 and contains a link_token field. If 422 (validation error), record the error detail.

If the accountability link was created successfully, verify GET http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/accountability/links now includes the new entry. Navigate back to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/dashboard and return to /accountability — verify the page still loads and shows the link. Take a screenshot.

description: [BEHAVIORAL] Flow E — Accountability digest API — verify digest and reply endpoints

steps.description: Load saved CEO session from '/home/ouroborous/code/phronex-test-runner/.tmp/comc-trunk-ceo-state.json' using the browser storage state tool. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/accountability. Verify the page loads.

Get all accountability links via browser_network_request: GET http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/accountability/links. If the array is non-empty, capture the first link_token for use in subsequent steps. If empty, the remaining steps will test the API endpoints with a placeholder token to verify correct error responses.

Test the partner digest endpoint (no auth required): use browser_network_request to GET http://localhost:8004/api/v1/accountability/digest/test_token_invalid with no Authorization header. This endpoint is partner-facing and must handle invalid tokens gracefully — verify the response is 404 (not 500 or 200 with data). If a real link_token was captured in step 2, use that instead and verify 200 with initiative data.

Test the replies endpoint: use browser_network_request to POST http://localhost:8004/api/v1/accountability/replies with body {"link_token": "invalid_token", "message": "test"} and no Authorization header. Verify the response is 404 (invalid token) or 422 (validation error), NOT 500 or 200 with data. The endpoint must reject invalid tokens without crashing.

Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/sessions (shows ComC sessions). Verify the page loads without error. Then navigate back to /accountability — confirm the page still displays correctly. Take a screenshot of the accountability page.

description: [BEHAVIORAL] Flow C — CRM contacts and interaction logging via portal and API

steps.description: Load saved CEO session from '/home/ouroborous/code/phronex-test-runner/.tmp/comc-trunk-ceo-state.json' using the browser storage state tool. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/crm. Verify the CRM page loads without 500 error or login redirect.

Verify the contacts list via browser_network_request: GET http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/crm/contacts. The response must be an array. If non-empty, capture the first contact's id for use in step 4. If empty, the CRM has no contacts yet.

If contacts list is empty, test creating a contact: POST http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/crm/contacts with body {"name": "JourneyHawk Test Contact", "email": "jh-test@example.com"}. Verify the response is 201 and contains an id. If 422, record the validation error detail — it may indicate required fields differ.

If a contact_id is available (from step 2 or 3), log an interaction: POST http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/crm/contacts/{contact_id}/interactions with body {"interaction_type": "call", "notes": "JourneyHawk test call", "date": "2026-05-08"}. Verify the response is 201 or 200. Then GET http://localhost:3002/api/admin/command-centre/api/v1/crm/contacts/{contact_id}/interactions — verify the new interaction appears in the list.

Navigate back to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/crm and verify the CRM page still loads. Navigate to http://localhost:3002/command-centre/companies — verify it loads. Take a screenshot showing the current CRM or companies page state.
